# CANDIDATE: VIX_LOW_OPENING_RANGE_EXPANSION_LONG

**Filed:** 2026-07-09  
**Filer:** chef-nemotron (free-tier autonomous R&D)  
**Type:** new_trigger  
**Status:** DRAFT (NEEDS-RATIFICATION per Rule 9)

## Hypothesis

In low‑volatility conditions (VIX < 13), opening range expansions that occur on above‑average volume tend to persist. This edge exists because low VIX indicates subdued market fear, and a volume‑surge breakout of the opening range suggests institutional participation that can drive sustained momentum.

## Mechanism

Entry: If VIX < 13 and price breaks above the opening range high (ORH) with 5‑minute volume > 1.5× the average 5‑minute volume of the prior 20 bars, enter long at the break bar’s close.  
Exit: Stop at the opening range low (ORL), target 2R or trail 15% off the highest‑since‑entry price.  
Regime filters: Only consider trades between 09:30‑10:30 ET, and require the EMA ribbon not to be inverted (fast EMA > slow EMA) to avoid counter‑trend noise.
